messages:
riley: Heads up — hit a weird auth bug when rotating API keys for long-lived python Client instances. Repro:
riley: 1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyA
riley: 2) client = Client()  # no explicit api_key
riley: 3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyB
riley: 4) subsequent client.request(...) still uses keyA until process restart
riley: Anyone seen this? :thinking:

maria: yep, seen similar. SDK caches headers on a global session object in a way that doesn't pick up env changes. short term: create new Client(api_key=os.environ[...]) when key rotates.

dan: can you paste the minimal repro? also which SDK version?

riley: sdk==0.9.3. minimial:

riley: ```python
riley: import os
riley: from redwood_inference import Client
riley:
riley: os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'A'
riley: c1 = Client()
riley: # rotate
riley: os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'B'
riley: c1.generate('hello')  # still uses key A
riley: ```

sam: oh interesting — Client() currently builds an aiohttp/requests.Session once and copies auth from env at construction. If the session stores Authorization header on a shared adapter, later env changes won't matter.

maria: also saw this interact badly with multiple clients in same process: creating Client(api_key='X') then later Client() picks up env but sometimes shares the session headers across instances because of a module-level session singleton. bug.

dan: workaround: explicitly pass api_key to every Client and avoid relying on env for long-running processes. adding a Client.update_api_key(new_key) would be nice.

riley: filing a quick issue with reproduction now. would like the SDK to support 3 things:
riley: - per-instance auth (no global mutable session headers)
riley: - an explicit rotate/update API (sync+async)
riley: - documented env-var precedence (explicit param > env at init > env reload?)

sam: +1. for async users we need both sync Client and AsyncClient parity. right now AsyncClient has slightly different init signature and missing the api_key kwarg in some overloads (typing makes it messy).

maria: typing note: current stubs use Union[str, None] for api_key but there are overloads that accept *requests.Session like objects. mypy complains.

dan: proposal: implement Client.update_api_key and AsyncClient.update_api_key async def, and change session management to be instance-local. we'll keep a module-level helper for default config but not session.

riley: also request: rotation hook / callback so infra can rotate keys pushed from vault and just call client.rotate_callback() or similar to update internal header atomically.

sam: CI bot run showed a test failing when multiple clients constructed in same process on top of our internal E2E suite. tagging @eng-ml and @eng-runtime for visibility.

ci-bot: New issue created: GH#4572 "python SDK: client reuses global session headers, breaks API key rotation and multi-client isolates" (link: https://git.internal/r/4572)

maria: small doc suggestion: add a short snippet in quickstart about long-running processes and key rotation. lots of users assume env var flips magically.

dan: I'll pick up the fix. plan: make session instance-local, add update_api_key sync/async, add tests for env-switch and multiple instances. will also add typing overloads to harmonize AsyncClient.

riley: thanks! can we also add a short migration note in CHANGELOG so folks know to stop relying on module-level session singletons?

dan: yep. PR will include changelog entry + upgrade note.

sam: leaving a :+1: for the feature request. if anyone in this thread wants to review the PR ping me.

riley: cheers, will follow up once issue has a PR.
